extracted.intended_audience: agencies preparing regulatory agendas, regulated stakeholders, and interested members of the public (regulatory stakeholders)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for what the Department of Education's Unified Agenda entries must contain and how the agenda is produced and presented (abstracts, timetables, legal citations, contacts, and regulatory-flexibility information). Useful for agencies drafting agenda items and for members of the public interpreting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda entry core elements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each set of regulations listed, the agenda provides the title of the document, the type of document, a citation to any rulemaking or other action taken since publication of the most recent agenda, and planned dates of future rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required listing item for each regulation set in the Unified Agenda; use consistent identification and cite prior actions and planned dates so the public can track progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An abstract that includes a description of the problem to be addressed, any principal alternatives being considered, and potential costs and benefits of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should succinctly state the problem, list principal alternatives under consideration, and outline anticipated costs and benefits to inform public participation and comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small-entity economic impact indication
rubrics_metrics.description: An indication of whether the planned action is likely to have significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities as defined by the Regulatory Flexibility Act (5 U.S.C. 601(6)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agenda entries must state whether a regulatory flexibility analysis is required and signal potential impacts on small entities to comply with the RFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to current CFR location
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference to where a reader can find the current regulations in the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise CFR title and part numbers (and any relevant subparts) so readers can locate existing regulatory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of legal authority
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List statutory and other legal authorities that authorize the agency action (e.g., specific U.S. Code sections, public laws) to show the basis for the proposed regulatory activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: The name, address, and telephone number of the contact person at ED from whom a reader can obtain additional information regarding the planned action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a specific agency contact (name, office, room, mailing address, phone, and email when available) and accommodations (e.g., relay services) so stakeholders can obtain clarifications and submit inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable / action schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: A timetable that lists planned actions (e.g., Notice of Intent to Commence Negotiated Rulemaking, NPRM, NPRM Comment Period End) with dates and FR citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include action labels, dates, and Federal Register citation lines where applicable so the public can track the regulatory milestones; note that dates are subject to revision in subsequent agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Analysis flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement whether a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis is required (e.g., 'Regulatory Flexibility Analysis Required: Yes').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly mark whether the analysis is required and, when applicable, provide links or references to the analysis to demonstrate compliance with the Regulatory Flexibility Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document heading content
rubrics_metrics.description: Document headings should contain the agency or agencies that issued and signed a document; the number of the CFR title and the number of each part the document amends, proposes to amend, or is directly related to; the agency docket number / agency internal file number; and the RIN which identifies each regulatory action listed in the Unified Agenda of Federal Regulatory and Deregulatory Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Document Drafting Handbook for detailed heading structure; headings also serve as navigational anchors but their repetition for navigation has no substantive legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for regulating (decision standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with ED's Principles for Regulating, ED is committed to regulations that improve the quality and equality of services it provides to its customers. ED will regulate only if absolutely necessary and then in the most flexible, most equitable, and least burdensome way possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency actions and proposed rules should be assessed against these principles; the public is invited to comment if items are inconsistent with these Principles for Regulating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment invitation on consistency and section 610 reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Interested members of the public are invited to comment on any of the items listed in this agenda that they believe are not consistent with the Principles for Regulating. Members of the public are also invited to comment on any uncompleted actions in this agenda that ED plans to review under section 610 of the Regulatory Flexibility Act to determine their economic impact on small entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When soliciting comments, explicitly flag items subject to Principle-consistency review and section 610 review so commenters can focus input on those matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic publication and access
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire Unified Agenda is published electronically and is available online at www.reginfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide links to machine-readable formats (JSON, XML, MODS) and official PDF versions (govinfo.gov) and note that the XML web rendition is an unofficial informational resource until ACFR grants it official legal status; researchers should verify against official editions.
